claims.text: Burn rate is the bad share of an SLI over a period divided by the share the SLO allows to be bad (1 − SLO); at a burn rate of 1 the error budget runs out exactly at the end of the SLO's window.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/alerts.md lines 27-28 at stage-4; Site Reliability Workbook, Alerting on SLOs (burn rate definition)

claims.text: Bad share = 1 − SLI; allowed share = 1 − SLO: 0.5% for S1 and S3 (SLO 99.5%), 1% for S2 and S4 (SLO 99%); S1 failed order placements, S2 slow order placements, S3 failed product reads, S4 slow refund requests; the window is a rolling 28 days.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/slo.md SLI table (lines 20-27), SLO table and window (lines 58-67), Error budget section at stage-4

claims.text: 28 days = 672 hours. The budget lasts the window divided by the burn rate: burn rate 2 → 14 days; 6 → about 4.7 days; 3 → about 9.3 days; 8 → 3.5 days; 16 → 1.75 days. One hour at burn rate b spends b/672 of the budget.
claims.source_hint: Arithmetic from alerts.md line 30 (28 days, 672 hours) and the definition in claim 1

claims.text: A 3% bad share is a burn rate of 6 against a 0.5% allowance (S3) and 3 against a 1% allowance (S2); 1% bad is 2 against 99.5% and 1 against 99%; 8% bad is 16 for S1 and 8 for S4. The 3% values in the situation are hypothetical.
claims.source_hint: Arithmetic from claim 1 and slo.md lines 64-67

claims.text: alerts.md fast level: 2% of the budget in 1 hour = 0.02 × 672 = 13.44; kept up, the 28-day budget lasts about 50 hours. Slow level: 5% in 6 hours = 0.05 × 672 / 6 = 5.6; budget gone in 5 days.
A burn rate becomes an SLI's threshold bad share by multiplying by 1 − SLO: 13.44 × 0.5% = 6.72% for S1 and S3, 13.44 × 1% = 13.44% for S2 and S4 (alerts.md writes S3's as about 6.7%).
claims.source_hint: docs/design/alerts.md lines 37-39 and alert table lines 53-60 at stage-4

claims.text: The thresholds 13.44 and 5.6 are the project's choice recomputed for a 28-day window, not a general standard.
Each level in alerts.md checks a long window (1 h, 6 h) and a short one (5 min, 30 min) together; the reason for the short window is left to devops.l4.burn-rate-alerts.

A burn rate of 6 for 6 hours spends 6 × 6 / 672, about 5.4% of the budget, more than one hour at 13.44 (2%); it stays below the fast threshold but above the slow one (5.6), so the slow level catches it and the fast one a sudden failure.

The b/672 conversion assumes requests arrive evenly over the window; the budget is a fixed number of bad requests (1 − SLO of all requests in 28 days), so a bad hour at peak traffic spends more of it than the same bad share at a quiet hour.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/slo.md Error budget section (budget counted in requests, 1 − SLO of the requests); arithmetic

claims.text: If S3's SLO were 99.9%, the fast threshold 13.44 would be about 1.3% bad over an hour (13.44 × 0.1%); with a 30-day (720-hour) window, 2% of the budget in an hour is a burn rate of 14.4.
claims.source_hint: Arithmetic from claim 1 (hypothetical changes, not in slo.md)

claims.text: A burn rate below 1 (e.g. 0.3% bad for S3 = 0.6), if kept, leaves budget at the end of the window.
When SLIs have different SLOs, compare bad shares through burn rate rather than one fixed percentage; one fixed percentage fits only when there is one SLI or all SLOs are equal.
claims.source_hint: Site Reliability Workbook, Alerting on SLOs; alerts.md writes thresholds per SLI

claims.text: slo.rules.yml records each SLI's bad share over 5 min, 30 min, 1 h and 6 h; job:product_reads_bad:ratio_rate1h and job:order_placement_slow:ratio_rate1h hold the 1-hour bad share of S3 and S2.
claims.source_hint: deploy/gitops/config-repo/platform/monitoring/rules/slo.rules.yml at stage-4 (ratio_rate5m, 30m, 1h, 6h per SLI; lines 18-19 and 79-80)

claims.text: A fixed bad-share threshold is a different burn rate per SLO: set to suit S2 and S4 (13.44%) it is a burn rate of 26.88 for S1 and S3, too late; set to suit S1 and S3 (6.72%) it is 6.72 for S2 and S4, too early.
claims.source_hint: Arithmetic from claim 1 and alerts.md alert table lines 53-60 at stage-4
